source.title: Stochastic Meta-Unlearning: Bridging Language Backbone and Multimodal Unlearning
source.authors: Zi-Jie Liu; Jinhao Duan; Gaowen Liu; Sijia Liu; Tian-Long Chen

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether text-side unlearning remains effective after recomposition into a VLM and image-conditioned evaluation. This is a conceptual test of recovery through a different input route, not a test of the listed fine-tuning, activation-ablation, quantization, or text-prompt attacks.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports that text-side unlearning can lower Forget Text accuracy while image-conditioned VLM queries often retain access to the target. Table 1 also reports unlearning outcomes in text-only and multimodal settings. Cited results from prior work are not recorded. Other table cells are omitted where the flattened text does not unambiguously assign values to models and settings.
record.test_reason: The study moves unlearning into a new setting: VLMs on meme classification. It reports forget accuracy for GradDiff, NPO and RMU under text-only and image-conditioned evaluation (Table 1). This bears on whether forgetting holds and on whether an input-side change (adding the image) restores the target. That is closest to E, as a new input route rather than rephrasing, and to A. Its main contribution, SMU, is the authors' own method and is not tested against the claim's listed attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that language-backbone unlearning verified only on text may not hold after VLM recomposition. They conclude that SMU, using VLM-level feedback in a bilevel meta-learning loop, gives the best forget-retain trade-off and transfers across targets and operators. The caveat about stronger adversarial prompts and unseen multimodal contexts comes from the Limitations and Broader Impact sections, not the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes bilevel meta-learning of a language-backbone initialization using multimodal outer-loop feedback. It compares GradDiff, NPO, and RMU, but does not reproduce the original unlearning-recovery attacks in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome differs across text-only versus image-conditioned evaluation, datasets, models, and unlearning methods; the paper reports especially poor utility for some GradDiff settings.
record.problems: The evidence is limited to two VLMs and two meme datasets. The cross-modal recovery description is qualitative in Figure 1, and the authors state that they do not establish resistance to stronger adversarial prompts or unseen multimodal contexts. Some table values are difficult to assign from the flattened text, so only values explicitly identified in the prose are included.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 1 cells are not extracted where the flattened table text does not unambiguously align values with model, method, dataset, and evaluation setting. Figures 4–6 discuss target and operator transfer for SMU, not recovery under the attacks in the claim.

untested.parts: The claim's simple attacks (relearning fine-tuning, quantization, activation ablation, rephrasing or jailbreak prompts) are not run. The tasks are meme classification, not factual or hazardous knowledge.
Not tested: no relearning or fine-tuning after unlearning.
Not tested: no direction ablation or deletion-versus-blocking analysis.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context facts are not tested. Only adding the image at inference is tested.
SMU is not evaluated against the listed recovery attacks. Its only robustness evidence is the text→multi evaluation and transfer across targets and operators.

missing.what: Full Text→Text versus Text→Multi Forget, Retain and Test for all baselines: Qwen Hateful NPO/RMU, Qwen Covid all methods, InternVL Covid all methods, InternVL Hateful GradDiff (46.67→64.07). Needed to judge E across settings.

Pre-unlearning finetuned Forget accuracy, giving the reference for how much unlearning removed. Hateful: image 92.93, MM 92.61. Covid: image 84.39, MM 81.41. Also image-side NPO/RMU leave high Forget (64–73 on Hateful).

record.verdict_notes: Mapping image-conditioned evaluation to E is my judgement: it is an inference-time input change with no weight edit, not prompting as such. Several caveats weaken the cross-modal evidence. RQ1 calls GradDiff/NPO/RMU 'direct VLM-side' baselines, yet Table 1 labels the columns Text→Text and Text→Multi, so whether the baselines were backbone-only unlearning is unclear. There is no InternVL pre-unlearning reference, so a text→multi rise could reflect task difficulty differences rather than recovery. Table 2's image-side GradDiff/NPO/RMU Hateful numbers are identical to Table 1's Qwen Hateful cells, suggesting a copy error. Forget accuracy here is classification accuracy on a held-out cluster (chance about 50% binary, 33% three-class), so values near 0 indicate collapse, not chance. The study is a method paper, and no original source is involved.

versions.untested_parts: Tests text-side unlearning followed by image-conditioned VLM evaluation on two meme datasets; does not test the listed attacks individually or establish recovery of factual knowledge beyond these classification tasks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is used to test recovery.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit analysis tests recovery or deletion versus blocked access.
No quantization of unlearned weights is tested.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context-information prompt attack is tested; image-conditioned inputs are tested instead.
SMU is evaluated for transfer across forgetting targets and unlearning operators, not for resistance to the attacks listed in the claim.

relation.reason: Reports Forget/Retain/Test for GradDiff, NPO and RMU under text-only and image-conditioned evaluation.

tranche.reason: New setting: VLMs on meme classification. Table 1's GradDiff/NPO/RMU baselines give results on whether forgetting holds under image-conditioned queries. SMU, the paper's own method, is not the evidence.

source_check.notes: Table 2 (Appendix B, image-side unlearning, model not named) repeats Table 1's Qwen baseline cells exactly for Text→Text and nearly for Text→Multi. RQ1 calls the baselines 'direct VLM-side', yet the caption says Text→Multi is after recomposition, so it is unclear what produced the Qwen baseline numbers. Hateful is a binary task and Covid a 3-class task.

statements.correction: Drop the 2607.18615 citation. Its cells with no rise are either collapsed GradDiff (Qwen Hateful Forget 2.02→0.87) or Covid, where Text→Multi Retain/Test for every baseline fall to 0.00–34.11 on a 3-class task. None shows resistance to recovery.
statements.problem: The statement says nothing about this study but cites r8. r8 is a GradDiff Qwen model the authors call collapsed (Text→Multi Retain 31.16, Test 40.20, below binary chance). Image-conditioned evaluation is neither a paraphrase nor a jailbreak.

statements.correction: Same-method contrast on Hateful Memes, NPO: InternVL3-8B 39.41→73.30 against Qwen2.5-VL-7B 64.07→64.21. Qwen NPO's Text→Text Forget (64.07) is not below its Test (62.20), so Qwen shows no forgetting to recover.
statements.problem: No number is given for this study. The cited rows pair different methods (r2 is NPO on InternVL, r8 is GradDiff on Qwen), so they don't show the same method across models, and r8's model is collapsed.
